reviews.review: Don't take this game too seriously and you will fall in love. Some of you may not find it worth $60 so if you have ANY doubts then i'd recommend you wait for a sale. It does have loads of content though. I've played 33 hours (at time of me writing this) and I don't think i'm close to beating the campaign yet.

[h1]For those new to the EDF franchise...[/h1]
This game is a great place to start. It offers a lot of great quality of life improvements over previous titles, while also rebooting the storyline. As such, despite being the latest game in a long franchise, you won't be missing any context or story from previous games. 

As for the game itself, it's just a lot of fun. It is insanely over the top, and inspired heavily by B-movies, and is all the better for it. It doesn't take itself at all seriously, and is just [i]fun[/i] the whole way through. The controls are pretty smooth (except for helicopters), and the graphics are decent for what you get: huge maps with no mid-mission loading screens, probably over a hundred enemies and allies all active on the map at once at times, and fully destructible buildings everywhere, and all without requiring a supercomputer to run. 

The only downside is that this game can be very grindy. If you want to 100% the game, you need to play through the entire story with all 4 classes, on all 5 difficulties (though Hard also counts as beating Easy and Normal). As this game has 110 missions, this means that to get all the achievements you will need to play 1320 missions, minimum. To get and fully upgrade every weapon in the game, you'll likely need to play far more than even that.

If you don't care about completion, though, the game isn't that grindy to just beat the game. Normal mode is designed to be able to play through without any grind at all (but be sure to pick up as many armor and weapon drops as possible during the missions). Hard is designed to be possible to beat from the beginning, and be a reasonable challenge after beating Normal. (Hardest and Inferno are only unlocked after beating the game, and virtually require beating Hard at least once to have high enough level gear to survive.)

Overall, this game is just a really fun shooter, and has a great online mode and online community. I fully recommend it.

[h1]For those coming from EDF 4.1...[/h1]
EDF5 has a lot of good quality-of-life improvements. It has some flaws to be sure, but overall it is mostly an improvement. A list of some important changes follow:

[b]General[/b]
+ Vehicles are now summoned using a separate button (A on an Xbox controller), and so don't take up space in your weapon sets
+ You now split armor and weapons among [i]all[/i] classes, not just the one you're playing. The active class gets the majority of weapons and usually the most armor awards, but you don't have to jump into Inferno with a new class and nothing but level 0 weapons if you main something else.
+ / - Weapons can now be upgraded by getting duplicates that have a higher stat. On one hand, this means you can still get some improvements when weapon farming even without getting the exact weapon you wanted. On the other hand, it also means that if you want to max out everything (or even a single specific weapon) there's now a lot [i]more[/i] grinding rather than just getting the weapon in the first place. 
+ Most classes have some way to increase their item pickup range. Rangers can sprint, wing divers can dash, Fencers can boost or dash, and all vehicles have a large pickup zone around them. 
- The voice acting isn't quite as good; it's less "B movie" and more just "not great"
+ Arguably a better story (it certainly engaged me more than than 4.1)
+ A few new enemy types

[b]Ranger[/b]
+ Rangers get a special equipment slot to further customize them beyond just their weapons
+ One option for special equipment is a number of vehicles, from actually usable bikes to railguns and tanks, even helicopters
+ Get a sprint option that extends pickup range and also gives a good option for covering ground quickly (faster and more convenient than rolling everywhere)

[b]Wing Diver[/b]
+ Many weapons are charged by the player before firing, which allows better tactical use along with flying
+ Can upgrade flight core to power more powerful weapons, even to the point of practically unlimited fire for a core of higher level than the weapon
- LAZR's (now "Mag Blasters") lose damage as their clip empties, meaning you have to constantly recharge them to keep their damage up (but they are arguably more powerful now when fully charged)

[b]Air Raider[/b]
+ GREATLY improved airstrike mechanics: 
     + Most gunship strikes and satellite lasers are now on a cooldown instead of requiring credits. For some (like the gunship autocannon), this cooldown is only about 1-2 seconds, allowing it to be used almost like a standard weapon with a unique firing angle.
     + Bombing runs now let you place the bombing path on the map yourself, no more smoke grenades with the vague hope that your line of cluster bombs hits vaguely where you wanted. 
- Greatly reduced vehicle options. No more Air Raider railguns. Most of the purely offensive vehicles were transferred exclusively to Ranger, including the Nereid helicopters, railguns, and a new type of massive damage vehicle (the EMC). Air Raiders still get a full array of tanks (including the Titans), Eros helicopters, the Balam analogue, and all the mecha varieties (including the depth crawlers).
+ Air Raiders now get 3 weapon/equipment slots, not including the vehicle. It's really nice to be able to have some kind of airstrike, a limpet gun, [i]and[/i] some kind of support equipment.

[b]Fencer[/b]
+ Fencers get two additional slots for various powerups, which can include extra dashes, shield improvements, recoil reduction, and faster turning rates. 
- Dash-cancelling seems to have been fixed, so no more near-infinite dashing
+ Dashing and boosting both create an item pick-up zone which makes collecting loot [i]much[/i] easier.

So overall, if you love 4.1 and aren't sure if you want to get 5, I would totally recommend it. 5 has tons of quality of life improvements as noted, and is just a great continuation of the franchise (even if the story itself is more of a reboot).
